subject.title: fix: antml:/mm: namespaced tool-call XML leaks into chat replies (#97750)

question: Should shared visible-text and persisted-history cleanup treat standalone `antml:`/`mm:` invoke XML and `<function_calls>`-wrapped invoke XML as leaked tool-call data while preserving bare invoke XML as user content?
rationale: The implementation and proof establish the known proxy-degradation behavior, but only a maintainer can choose whether the namespace/wrapper signature is sufficient justification for irreversible deletion from durable transcripts across all channels.

options.title: Adopt the qualified-leak boundary
options.body: Accept the narrow allow-list for delivery and persisted history because the known degradation carries a namespace or wrapper signature and bare examples remain preserved.

options.title: Limit removal to delivery
options.body: Strip qualified markup from user-facing replies but retain it verbatim in persisted history if transcript fidelity has priority.

options.title: Pause for provider-owned recovery
options.body: Defer this sanitizer policy if degraded invoke text should instead be classified or recovered through provider-specific metadata or execution handling.

recommendation.title: Adopt the qualified-leak boundary
recommendation.body: Accept the narrow allow-list for delivery and persisted history because the known degradation carries a namespace or wrapper signature and bare examples remain preserved.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans shared runtime text policy and durable transcript semantics rather than a contributor-local implementation detail.
